name: Gilbert Hill
role: Privacy Technologist & Commissioner, UK Data & Marketing Regulator
title: The Trust Dividend: How Ethical AI Outperforms Creepy Marketing Every Time
synopsis: In this session, privacy technologist and entrepreneur Gilbert Hill will bust the myth that data ethics kills conversion rates. We will explore how clean, zero-party data and transparent AI guardrails actually yield higher-quality leads, eliminate algorithmic bias that wastes ad spend, and build fierce customer loyalty. You’ll come away with a practical framework for auditing your marketing AI stack to ensure it’s driving revenue, not regulatory risk.

name: Rasmus Houlind
role: Author of Hello $Firstname and CXO at Agillic
title: Beyond Hello $Firstname – The Real Meaning of Personalization and How AI Helps Scale It
synopsis: This keynote cuts through the noise around personalization and explains, in practical terms, what it actually is. Drawing on Hello $Firstname and the Bowtie of Personalization, the session shows marketers how to work with personalization in a structured way across campaigns, automation, and digital experiences, while avoiding the common traps that waste time and budget.

The keynote also confronts the real impact of generative AI. Participants learn how AI removes the content bottleneck, how it can finally scale personalization in a meaningful way, and where the biggest risks appear when teams rush in without the right structure or understanding.
In thirty minutes, the audience gets a clear definition of personalization and a realistic view of how AI can elevate it from ambition to execution.

name: Valeriya Pilkevich
title: Beyond Personal Productivity: Building Agentic Marketing Teams That Actually Compound
synopsis: Over 80% of companies report zero measurable productivity gains from AI – even as their employees swear by it. Individual AI wins aren’t compounding into company wins, and marketing teams feel this acutely: every marketer running their own prompts, their own version of the ICP, their own brand voice, their own playbooks. The productivity stays personal. The leverage never reaches the P&L.

This session is for marketing leaders ready to move past tool-by-tool experimentation and start building agentic marketing teams — where AI agents work from shared organizational context, not 30 private chat histories. We’ll cover both halves of the equation: the practical (a live demo of Claude as a marketing co-worker, operating from a team’s shared brand, ICP, and campaign context) and the strategic (the governance, guardrails, and operating-model decisions you need so this scales without creating new risk).
You’ll leave with a clear picture of what a real agentic marketing team looks like – and the three decisions you need to make before you build one.
